purpose: Attach a filesystem. Without args, lists current mounts (read /proc/mounts). With one arg, mounts per /etc/fstab entry.

flags.name: -t TYPE
flags.doc: Filesystem type. auto attempts detection. tmpfs, ext4, xfs, btrfs, nfs, cifs, overlay, etc.

flags.name: -o OPTIONS
flags.doc: Comma-separated mount options. Common: rw/ro, exec/noexec, suid/nosuid, dev/nodev, atime/noatime/relatime, sync/async, defaults. FS-specific: data=ordered (ext4), barrier (ext4/xfs), discard, etc.

flags.name: --bind
flags.doc: Bind mount (= -o bind). Same inode visible at second path.

flags.name: --move
flags.doc: Atomically move a mount to a new location.

flags.name: -O OPTIONS
flags.doc: With -a: only mount fstab entries with matching options.

flags.name: --source DEV
flags.doc: Explicit source (helps when target alone is given).

examples.scenario: Remount root RW after rescue boot.
Make docker storage available at second path with shared propagation.

purpose: Detach a filesystem. Returns EBUSY if files open / processes have CWD inside.

flags.name: -f
flags.doc: Force (try harder for NFS hangs). May not actually free resources if processes still hold.

flags.name: -l, --lazy
flags.doc: Lazy unmount: detach immediately, clean up when last user closes. The 'I'll deal with it later' option.

flags.name: -r
flags.doc: On failure, try to remount RO.

flags.name: -R
flags.doc: Recursive — also unmount any sub-mounts under MOUNTPOINT.

examples.scenario: Try clean unmount, fall back to lazy if busy.

purpose: Tree view of block devices: disks → partitions → LVs → filesystems. Shows MAJ:MIN, SIZE, RO, TYPE, MOUNTPOINTS.

flags.name: -f, --fs
flags.doc: Show FSTYPE, FSVER, LABEL, UUID, FSAVAIL, FSUSE%.

flags.name: -o COLS
flags.doc: Custom columns (NAME, MAJ:MIN, RM, SIZE, RO, TYPE, MOUNTPOINTS, FSTYPE, LABEL, UUID, MODEL, SERIAL, ROTA, ZONED, ...).

flags.name: -D
flags.doc: Discard info (TRIM support, granularity, max bytes).

examples.scenario: Inventory of disks + filesystems on the host.

purpose: Print block device attributes: UUID, LABEL, TYPE. Reads superblock signatures. Used by udev rules and /etc/fstab UUID resolution.

flags.name: -n LIST
flags.doc: Restrict probing to these FS types.

flags.name: -o FORMAT
flags.doc: Output: full (default), value, list, device, udev, export.

flags.name: -s TAG
flags.doc: Show only this tag (TYPE, UUID, LABEL, etc.).

examples.scenario: Find which device has a given UUID.

purpose: Manage loop devices. Set up a /dev/loopN backed by a regular file (disk image, encrypted container, etc.).

flags.name: -f, --find
flags.doc: Find first free /dev/loopN. With FILE, attach + return name. With --show, print the picked name.

flags.name: -P, --partscan
flags.doc: Scan for partitions on the loop image.

examples.scenario: Mount a disk image with partition scanning.

flags.name: -c
flags.doc: Check device for bad blocks before creating.

flags.name: -i BYTES_PER_INODE
flags.doc: Inode density. Default ~16K. Smaller = more inodes (more files allowed).

flags.name: -O FEATURES
flags.doc: Comma-separated FS features. Common: ^has_journal (no journal), ^huge_file, casefold, encrypt, project.

flags.name: -E EXTENDED_OPTS
flags.doc: Extended options. e.g. stride=,stripe-width= for RAID; lazy_itable_init=1 (faster mkfs, slower first use).

flags.name: -T USAGE_TYPE
flags.doc: Tune defaults for usage: news, largefile, largefile4, hurd, big, default.

flags.name: -n
flags.doc: Show what would be done (don't actually create).

flags.name: -d DIR
flags.doc: Pre-populate FS with contents of DIR.

examples.expected_output: creates ext4 with label, fast init

purpose: Adjust ext2/3/4 filesystem parameters. Most operations require the FS unmounted.

flags.name: -i INTERVAL
flags.doc: Time between forced fsck. e.g. 30d, 6m. 0 = disable.

flags.name: -e ERROR_BEHAVIOR
flags.doc: continue|remount-ro|panic. What to do on FS error.

flags.name: -u USER
flags.doc: User who can use reserved blocks.

flags.name: -g GROUP
flags.doc: Group who can use reserved blocks.

flags.name: -O FEATURES
flags.doc: Enable/disable FS features. Prefix ^ to disable.

examples.scenario: Inspect FS state, last fsck, mount count, features.
Disable time/mount-based forced fsck (modern systems use journal recovery).

purpose: Create XFS filesystem. Modern XFS is the default for RHEL 7+ rootfs.

flags.name: -d OPTIONS
flags.doc: Data section: agcount= (allocation groups for parallelism), agsize=, file=, name= (image filename), size=, sunit= (RAID stripe unit), swidth= (RAID stripe width), su=, sw=.

flags.name: -l OPTIONS
flags.doc: Log section: agnum=, internal=, logdev=, size= (default ~64MB), su=, version=, sectsize=.

flags.name: -n OPTIONS
flags.doc: Naming options: ftype=1 (default — needed for overlayfs), size=.

flags.name: -i OPTIONS
flags.doc: Inode options: size= (256/512/1024/2048), maxpct=, attr=, projid32bit=.

flags.name: -m OPTIONS
flags.doc: Metadata options: crc=1 (default — checksums), finobt=1, rmapbt=, reflink=1 (default — for cp --reflink).

examples.scenario: Tuned for many-CPU host with heavy parallel IO.

purpose: Create Btrfs filesystem. Multi-device aware: pass multiple DEVICES for built-in RAID.

flags.name: -m PROFILE
flags.doc: Metadata profile: single, raid0, raid1, raid5, raid6, raid10, dup.

flags.name: -O FEATURES
flags.doc: Enable features: extref, skinny-metadata, no-holes, raid56, free-space-tree, raid1c34, mixed-bg.

purpose: LVM2 main entry — interactive shell or CLI. In practice, individual binaries (pvcreate, vgcreate, lvcreate, etc.) are invoked. lvm itself rarely run directly.

flags.name: pvs / vgs / lvs
flags.doc: List PVs / VGs / LVs in tabular form. -o customizes columns.

flags.name: lvextend -L +SIZE LV
flags.doc: Grow LV (then resize FS via fsadm or resize2fs/xfs_growfs).

purpose: Initialize disk/partition as LVM Physical Volume.

flags.name: --metadatacopies N
flags.doc: Number of metadata copies on this PV.

purpose: Create a Volume Group from one or more PVs.

flags.name: -s SIZE
flags.doc: Physical extent size (default 4M). Determines max LV size and granularity.

flags.name: -l EXTENTS
flags.doc: Size in extents (or %VG / %FREE / %PVS / %ORIGIN for snapshots). e.g. -l 100%FREE = use all free space.

flags.name: -i N
flags.doc: Stripe count (0 = no striping; 2+ = stripe across N PVs).

flags.name: -m N
flags.doc: Mirror copies (0 = no mirror; 1 = one mirror = 2 copies total).

flags.name: --type TYPE
flags.doc: Segment type: linear, striped, raid0/1/5/6/10, mirror, snapshot, thin, thin-pool, cache, cache-pool.

flags.name: --thinpool POOL
flags.doc: Use thin pool for thin provisioning.

examples.expected_output: 4-way striped LV using all free space

flags.name: luksFormat DEVICE
flags.doc: Initialize LUKS on device. Prompts for passphrase.

flags.name: luksOpen DEVICE NAME
flags.doc: Open device, create /dev/mapper/NAME. Prompts for passphrase.

flags.name: luksAddKey DEVICE
flags.doc: Add new passphrase to next slot.

flags.name: luksDump DEVICE
flags.doc: Show LUKS header (cipher, KDF, slot info).

flags.name: luksHeaderBackup --header-backup-file F DEVICE
flags.doc: Save LUKS header to file (critical: lose header = lose data even with passphrase).

flags.name: luksErase DEVICE
flags.doc: Wipe all keyslots (renders device unrecoverable; use carefully).

examples.invocation: cryptsetup luksFormat /dev/sdb1 && cryptsetup luksOpen /dev/sdb1 secure && mkfs.ext4 /dev/mapper/secure && mount /dev/mapper/secure /mnt/secure
examples.expected_output: encrypted volume created, opened, formatted, mounted
version, cipher, KDF, key slot info
